punchline: A whole business model fits in nine boxes, and moving one sticky note moves the ones around it.
thirty_sec: Alexander Osterwalder turned his doctoral work on business models into one sheet with nine boxes: customers, value, channels, relationships, revenue, resources, activities, partners and costs. A team prints it large, fills it with sticky notes and argues about one box at a time. Change the customer box and the channels and costs may have to move too. Critics point out that the sheet is a snapshot and says little about how a model changes over time.
